title: Create ServiceNow incident payload
description: Flat JSON body for POST /incidents; do not wrap fields in request_body. Create an incident after caller confirmation. Use a trusted 32-character caller_id, valid scope and impact enum values, and a semicolon-delimited string for attempted_steps. Do not include credentials, secrets, tokens, passwords, PINs, or unnecessary personal information.

caller_id.description: Trusted ServiceNow sys_user.sys_id for the authenticated caller. Do not generate or infer this value.

short_description.description: Plain-language issue summary without credentials, secrets, employee ID, unsupported diagnosis, or invented facts.

description.description: Redacted incident details: symptoms, exact error if known, timing, scope, impact, and troubleshooting attempted.
description.example: The external monitor stopped displaying this morning. The laptop display works.

work_notes.description: Optional internal ServiceNow work note. Do not include credentials, secrets, or unnecessary personal information.
work_notes.example: Initial triage was completed by the AI agent.

affected_item.description: Caller-stated affected device, application, or service. Omit when unknown; do not infer a configuration item.

error_message.description: Exact caller-stated error text after removing credentials or secrets.

started_when.description: Caller-stated time or relative period when the issue began. Do not invent a timestamp.

affected_scope.description: Scope explicitly supported by the caller's description. Use single_user when only the caller is affected, multiple_users when several users are affected, site_or_service for a site-wide or service-wide issue, or unknown when the scope is not established. The backend maps this to ServiceNow impact.

business_impact.description: Caller-stated work impact. Use work_blocked when the caller is unable to do any work, work_degraded when work is impaired but still possible, not_blocked when work is unaffected, or unknown when the impact is not established. The backend maps this to ServiceNow urgency.

attempted_steps.description: Troubleshooting steps already attempted, in order. Separate multiple steps with semicolons; whitespace around separators is ignored.
attempted_steps.example: Reconnected the cable; Restarted the dock

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-generated key used to recognize a repeated create request for the same caller. X-Idempotency-Key or X-Request-ID headers may be used instead.

caller_confirmed.description: True only after the caller explicitly confirms the final incident summary and asks to create it.
